cues.en: Welcome to Section two Introduction to Fraud Detection.
cues.zh: 歡迎來到第二章：詐欺偵測簡介。

cues.en: This is lecture three.
cues.zh: 這是第三堂課。

cues.en: What is anomaly detection?
cues.zh: 什麼是異常偵測？

cues.en: So if we look at this image with basically a massive tray full of eggs, the majority of them are white, as we know.
cues.zh: 看看這張圖片，整個大盤子裝滿了蛋，大多數都是我們熟悉的白色。

cues.en: And we can see one that sticks out, which is the red one.
cues.zh: 其中有一顆特別顯眼，就是這顆紅色的蛋。

cues.en: So in a sense, this red egg would be anomalous in relation to all of the other normal eggs that we know to be white.
cues.zh: 相較於其他正常的白色蛋，這顆紅色蛋就算是異常。

cues.en: And this can be cast as a machine learning problem in a sense.
cues.zh: 某種程度上，這可以轉換成機器學習問題。

cues.en: If it's fraud detection that we're speaking about, you know, we have very few fraudulent transactions.
cues.zh: 如果談的是詐欺偵測，詐欺交易通常非常少。

cues.en: We have a lot of normal transactions.
cues.zh: 正常交易則很多。

cues.en: But how do we go about training a model that can find these red eggs specifically within a sea of predominantly white eggs or normal transactions?
cues.zh: 那麼，要如何訓練模型，在以白色蛋，也就是正常交易為主的茫茫資料中，找出這些紅色蛋？

cues.en: So by means of a definition, an anomaly can be seen as data that deviates substantially from the norm.
cues.zh: 從定義上來說，異常就是明顯偏離常態的資料。

cues.en: And detecting anomalies.
cues.zh: 而異常偵測，

cues.en: It's the process of identifying rare observations that differ substantially from the majority of the data from where they are drawn.
cues.zh: 就是辨識罕見觀測值的過程，這些觀測值與其所屬資料中的大多數有明顯差異。

cues.en: So again, in a in a financial services context, by definition, if the majority of your transactions were fraudulent, you probably wouldn't be in business for very long.
cues.zh: 以金融服務為例，如果大部分交易都是詐欺，公司大概很快就無法經營了。

cues.en: So you can rest assured that most transactions are good for a company to remain in business because fraud is obviously expensive.
cues.zh: 因此，公司若能持續經營，就可以合理假設大部分交易是正常的，畢竟詐欺的代價很高。

cues.en: There's a lot of penalties, there's a lot of reputational risks, etcetera associated with it.
cues.zh: 詐欺會帶來許多罰則、聲譽風險等問題。

cues.en: But natural levels of fraud do exist within within most organizations.
cues.zh: 不過，大多數組織都會存在一定程度的詐欺。

cues.en: You almost need to keep a very low baseline of fraud.
cues.zh: 你幾乎只能把詐欺維持在非常低的基準水準。

cues.en: It's naturally a typical problem to solve, but you can never eliminate fraud completely because the problem is complex.
cues.zh: 這是經常需要處理的問題，但因為情況複雜，不可能完全消除詐欺。

cues.en: Bad actors are typically evolving.
cues.zh: 惡意行為者通常也會持續演變。

cues.en: They've got more sophisticated methodology, and as an organization, if you don't have kind of 100%
cues.zh: 他們的方法會愈來愈精密。而組織如果無法百分之百

cues.en: certainty in what is or isn't fraud, which you really are never going to achieve, typically you're
cues.zh: 確定哪些行為是詐欺、哪些不是，而實際上你永遠做不到完全確定，通常就會

cues.en: going to apply some sort of operational process to circumvent the fraud, which is a kind of friction
cues.zh: 採用某種營運流程來防止詐欺，但這也會造成操作上的阻力，

cues.en: which might make the customer experience a little bit slow.
cues.zh: 讓客戶的使用流程稍微變慢。

cues.en: Certain customers might not have access to features on your website, for example, and that also has a negative feedback or a negative experience on the customer.
cues.zh: 例如，有些客戶可能無法使用網站上的某些功能，這也會造成負面回饋或不好的客戶體驗。

cues.en: So in some sense, you're never going to apply full friction where you give your customers a bad experience.
cues.zh: 因此，你不會全面設下阻力，讓所有客戶都有不好的體驗。

cues.en: You'll have some some throughput of, of customers, you'll allow them some leniency.
cues.zh: 你仍要讓一定數量的客戶順利通過，給予他們一些彈性。

cues.en: But you're trying to solve this problem as intelligently as possible.
cues.zh: 但同時也要盡可能聰明地解決這個問題。

cues.en: So there's definitely a trade off in that sense.
cues.zh: 所以這當中確實存在取捨。

cues.en: And the applications of anomaly detection, I have spoken about fraud a few times.
cues.zh: 關於異常偵測的應用，剛剛我已多次提到詐欺。

cues.en: There are definitely many other applications.
cues.zh: 但它當然還有許多其他用途。

cues.en: Some include intrusion detection.
cues.zh: 其中包括入侵偵測。

cues.en: So, you know, website systems, things like that, getting hacked from a network perspective, fault
cues.zh: 例如，從網路角度偵測網站或系統遭到駭入，以及故障

cues.en: detection, health care monitoring systems, monitoring, predictive maintenance.
cues.zh: 偵測、醫療照護監控、系統監控與預測性維護。

cues.en: There's there's many, many application areas.
cues.zh: 應用領域非常多。

cues.en: When you think of the term anomaly, you might think of an outlier.
cues.zh: 聽到「異常」這個詞，你可能會想到離群值。

cues.en: And in some sense they are similar, but an anomaly.
cues.zh: 某種程度上，兩者很相似，但異常

cues.en: I'll give you an example of how that would differ from a numerical perspective.
cues.zh: 與離群值也有差別，我會從數值的角度舉例說明。

cues.en: So let's assume a distribution of data.
cues.zh: 假設有一組資料分布。

cues.en: We'll just create a very simple histogram and we'll assume a normal distribution with a mean of 100
cues.zh: 我們先畫一張簡單的直方圖，假設資料呈常態分布，平均數為 100，

cues.en: and for example, standard deviation of ten.
cues.zh: 標準差例如設為 10。

cues.en: So we could assume that this is a subset of IQ scores from within a population of some sort, but we
cues.zh: 可以把它想成某個群體抽取出來的一部分智商分數，不過

cues.en: luckily can generate that with numpy within Python.
cues.zh: 我們可以直接用 Python 的 NumPy 產生這些資料。

cues.en: So that's a library for numerical processing and we can specify our MU or our mean value as well as
cues.zh: NumPy 是做數值運算的函式庫，我們可以指定 mu，也就是平均數，

cues.en: our sigma or our standard deviation, and we're just going to call them 110.
cues.zh: 以及 sigma，也就是標準差，這裡分別設為 100 和 10。

cues.en: And then from within numpy I can randomly generate a distribution of numbers, a normal distribution
cues.zh: 接著透過 NumPy，依照剛才設定的參數，隨機產生一組

cues.en: as per these parameters that I've just set.
cues.zh: 符合常態分布的數值。

cues.en: So this mu value the sigma value.
cues.zh: 也就是依據 mu 和 sigma 的值。

cues.en: And I would like to sample 1000 data points.
cues.zh: 我想抽取 1,000 個資料點。

cues.en: And then lastly, I actually want to plot this as a as a distribution so I can make use of the matplotlib.
cues.zh: 最後，我想把資料畫成分布圖，因此可以使用 Matplotlib

cues.en: Barbary, which is a very popular library for creating plots within Python.
cues.zh: 函式庫，這是在 Python 中非常常用的繪圖函式庫。

cues.en: And it's as simple as calling the.
cues.zh: 只需要呼叫這個

cues.en: Library.
cues.zh: 函式庫。

cues.en: So the object.
cues.zh: 也就是這個物件。

cues.en: We're going to initialize a histogram.
cues.zh: 我們會建立一張直方圖。

cues.en: We're going to supply the randomly generated normal distribution values, which is s, which is assigned
cues.zh: 把隨機產生的常態分布數值，也就是指定給變數 s 的資料，

cues.en: to the variable S, and I'm going to burn them into 40 bins and I want to present the plot.
cues.zh: 傳進去，分成 40 個區間，然後顯示圖表。

cues.en: I want to expose it.
cues.zh: 我要把圖顯示出來。

cues.en: Let's see how it looks.
cues.zh: 看看結果如何。

cues.en: All right.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So we've got what appears to be a normal distribution or a simple bell curve, which we know from statistics
cues.zh: 這看起來就是常態分布，也就是統計學中常見的鐘形曲線，

cues.en: with a mean value of 100 and then a standard deviation of ten.
cues.zh: 平均數為 100，標準差為 10。

cues.en: So one standard deviation would be here, two standard deviations, three standard deviations, etcetera.
cues.zh: 這裡是一個標準差，接著是兩個標準差、三個標準差，依此類推。

cues.en: If we had to look for the outliers in the sense it would be the data points that sit at the very far tails on either side of the distribution.
cues.zh: 如果要找離群值，就是分布兩側尾端最遠的那些資料點。

cues.en: So the very high IQs or the very low IQs, those would be our outliers for this particular data point,
cues.zh: 也就是智商非常高或非常低的那些值，對這個資料變數而言，它們就是離群值，

cues.en: which within a data frame might just be a single column, right?
cues.zh: 而這個變數放在 DataFrame 裡，可能就只是一個欄位，對吧？

cues.en: But there are ways that we can set some sort of a threshold and say, well, if the data is above 120
cues.zh: 我們可以設定某種門檻，例如資料高於 120

cues.en: or 130, we can classify it as an outlier.
cues.zh: 或 130 時，就把它歸為離群值。

cues.en: And the same on the lower side.
cues.zh: 較低的一側也一樣。

cues.en: We can also just set a threshold.
cues.zh: 同樣可以直接設定門檻。

cues.en: Which works pretty well.
cues.zh: 這種方式的效果相當好。

cues.en: Then we also have the context of a box plot.
cues.zh: 另外還有盒鬚圖。

cues.en: And a box plot can print the very same data for us.
cues.zh: 盒鬚圖也可以呈現同一組資料。

cues.en: So let us have a look at what a box plot does.
cues.zh: 我們來看看盒鬚圖的作用。

cues.en: So box plot also represents the data, and it's a statistical technique for measuring the dispersion
cues.zh: 盒鬚圖同樣用來呈現資料，是衡量資料離散程度的統計方法，

cues.en: of our data, and it has a few different properties to it.
cues.zh: 其中包含幾個不同的特性。

cues.en: So firstly, the orange line is the median of our data and you can see against the y axis that the value
cues.zh: 首先，橘色線代表資料的中位數。對照 y 軸，可以看到

cues.en: of 100 perfectly lines up with the the median, which is what we set.
cues.zh: 中位數正好對應到 100，也就是我們設定的值。

cues.en: Then we've got the minimum value, which is the 25th percentile -1.5 on the of the interquartile range.
cues.zh: 接著是下界，也就是第 25 百分位數減去 1.5 倍的四分位距。

cues.en: So it's a soft minimum, it's not the actual minimum value, but rather it's a soft minimum based on this formula.
cues.zh: 這是依公式計算的軟性下界，並不是資料真正的最小值。

cues.en: And this value is effectively this bottom line over here.
cues.zh: 這個值實際上就對應到這裡最下面的這條線。

cues.en: Then we've got the maximum, which again is a soft maximum, which is the 75th percentile plus 1.5 times
cues.zh: 再來是上界，同樣是軟性上界，等於第 75 百分位數加上 1.5 倍

cues.en: the interquartile range, which is this this level up here, The interquartile range itself is effectively
cues.zh: 四分位距，也就是上面這個位置。四分位距本身則對應到

cues.en: this big rectangular block in the middle, which ranges from the 25th percentile.
cues.zh: 中間這個大的長方形區塊，範圍從第 25 百分位數

cues.en: So the 25th percentile value to the 75th percentile and then it builds a rectangle.
cues.zh: 一直到第 75 百分位數，形成一個長方形。

cues.en: I mean, the shape can differ.
cues.zh: 當然，它的形狀可能不同。

cues.en: It can become more of a square.
cues.zh: 也可能更接近正方形。

cues.en: And then these hard and.
cues.zh: 接著是這些所謂的硬性和，

cues.en: Soft, rather soft, max and min values.
cues.zh: 應該說是軟性上界與下界。

cues.en: Outliers can fall beyond that.
cues.zh: 離群值可能落在這些範圍之外。

cues.en: So if there's data points that fall beyond this maximum and minimum value, then these would be classed as outliers according to the box plot.
cues.zh: 如果資料點超過這個上界或下界，依照盒鬚圖的判定方式，它們就是離群值。

cues.en: So in this case, we've only really got one.
cues.zh: 在這個例子中，我們看起來只有一個。

cues.en: Maybe there's a few that are overlaid, but if we regenerate our distribution again, remember this is a random process.
cues.zh: 也可能有幾個點重疊了。不過，如果重新產生分布，別忘了這是隨機過程，

cues.en: We've got a different distribution that's plotted here.
cues.zh: 這裡畫出的分布就會不同。

cues.en: We see more outliers and this is just outliers according to the box plot methodology.
cues.zh: 我們會看到更多離群值，而這些都是依盒鬚圖方法判定的離群值。

cues.en: All right.
cues.zh: 好。

cues.en: So that works really well for a one dimensional data point.
cues.zh: 對於一維資料，這種方式非常有效。

cues.en: So just a single column of homogenous.
cues.zh: 也就是只有單一欄位、性質一致的

cues.en: Data, but for higher dimensional data.
cues.zh: 資料。但對於更高維度的資料，

cues.en: So for, for example, a set of features or a data frame of data, outliers and detecting those outliers
cues.zh: 例如一組特徵，或是一個 DataFrame，離群值及其偵測問題

cues.en: becomes too complicated for those approaches, these simple approaches.
cues.zh: 就太複雜，無法再用這些簡單方法處理。

cues.en: So then we often need to take a non-linear approach in order to detect those outliers or these anomalies
cues.zh: 因此，我們往往必須採用非線性方法來偵測這些離群值或異常，

cues.en: as we need to determine how the data differs with each other and how the data from different columns
cues.zh: 因為需要判斷資料彼此如何不同，以及特徵空間中不同欄位的資料

cues.en: in the feature space interacts with one another, which ultimately adds to the predictive ability of the approach.
cues.zh: 如何交互作用，而這些關係最終會影響方法的預測能力。

cues.en: So something that might seem like an outlier within a single column is easy to detect.
cues.zh: 如果某個值只在單一欄位中顯得異常，通常很容易偵測。

cues.en: I mean, we can just see it deviate very significantly from the the distribution of the data.
cues.zh: 我們可以直接看到它明顯偏離資料分布。

cues.en: But an outlier in a broader context might be slightly different data in 2 or 3 or four different variables
cues.zh: 但在更廣泛的情境下，異常可能是兩個、三個或四個變數各有些微差異，

cues.en: that collectively, when acting together, have this non-linear transformation that indicates anomalous
cues.zh: 它們一起作用時，透過非線性的組合，呈現出異常

cues.en: behavior, but which is not easy to detect if you're just looking at each of the columns in isolation.
cues.zh: 行為；如果只單獨查看各個欄位，這種情況就不容易察覺。
